posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
you don't.
just as an example:
every year a few users are asking for a way to have more than 999 maps - but completed games usually have less than 200 maps.
That is because it takes time to create good maps, and even professional teams do not have the time to create many hundred maps to make a game.
As an independent single developer you'll have absolutely no chance to solve that workload either, the only ones who post of making a dozen maps a weekend were always revealed as people using the random generator and barely adding to their large (and empty) maps.
and its similar for all other parts, especially if you just ask for breaking all limits.
Here is a better suggestion:
plan your game and make real  estimates of what you can and will do (no need to open the editor for planning). Think about writing an advertisement for your game - but one that doesn't use numbers or numeric superlatives.
Then check if you really have to break any limit for that game - if yes then ask for that specific limit and tell us what you need to break it for, and we will give you ways to handle that.
